title: The Smiley :-) (1982)
voice_direction: Kurt or Jade: dry, warm, lightly amused. Matter-of-fact on the hook, a small smile in 'Read it sideways', a beat of quiet on 'lost', final question light and genuinely curious.
narration: The smiley was invented because a joke backfired. In September nineteen eighty-two, someone on a Carnegie Mellon message board posted a mercury warning about an elevator. It was a joke, and some readers missed that. So on the nineteenth, a computer scientist named Scott Fahlman proposed a fix, in a short, casual note. A colon, a hyphen, and a bracket. Read it sideways, he wrote. That meant a joke. He suggested the frown for posts that were not. It caught on fast. But the original post was lost. In two thousand two, staff dug it out of old backup tapes, after hunting for a drive that could still read them. Even a smile can get lost. Smiley with a nose, or without?
question: Smiley with a nose, or without?

instagram_caption:
The smiley was invented because a joke backfired. 🙂

In September 1982, a Carnegie Mellon online bulletin board lit up over a warning that an elevator was contaminated with mercury. It was a joke, and some readers missed that.

On 19 September, computer scientist Scott Fahlman proposed marking jokes with a colon, a hyphen and a bracket, to be read sideways: :-) . He also suggested :-( for posts that were not jokes.

The original post was later lost. In 2002, CMU staff recovered it from old backup tapes (retrieved 10 September 2002).

answer: Nose, every time. :-) feels more finished to me, though I admit :) is faster.

facts.claim: Fahlman's post proposing :-) as a joke marker (and :-( for non-jokes, 'Read it sideways') dated 19 Sep 1982, 11:44, subject ':-)'

Mercury/elevator thread 16-17 Sep 1982: Howard Gayle's 'WARNING!' (16 Sep 17:21) about a mercury-contaminated elevator; Rudy Nedved (16 Sep 21:34) said it was a joke; Fahlman's own mock-alarming 'Elevators (*)' post 17 Sep. 'Some readers missed it' is inferred from the follow-ups; stay hedged
Original thread recovered by Jeff Baird from the Spice VAX October 1982 backup tape on 10 Sep 2002 (effort started Feb 2002 by Mike Jones; staff hunted for a tape drive that could read the media)
facts.source: CMU, Original Bboard Thread; Fahlman 'Smiley Lore' page (Digital Coelacanth Project)

facts.claim: Fahlman is 'credited with' the first smiley emoticon; earlier typographic smile ideas existed (1967 Reader's Digest, Nabokov 1969), so do NOT say 'first ever'
'It caught on fast' is general and unverified in detail here; dropped any specific spread dates
facts.source: not verified; Fahlman page says it spread
